body: Most homes in North Central Florida collect drywall damage gradually: a doorknob through the wall, nail pops along the ceiling, a cracked corner over a doorway, a soft spot under a leaking window. Our drywall repair service covers small fixes and larger sections in one visit, then paints the area so it blends instead of showing up as a shiny square.
If a leak has just happened and you need fast help, our post on urgent drywall repair in Newberry explains what to do while you wait.
bullets: Holes from doorknobs, anchors, moved fixtures, and plumbing access
Nail and screw pops along walls and ceilings
Stress cracks at door and window corners and ceiling joints
Water-stained or soft drywall from roof, AC, or plumbing leaks
Full sheet replacement where damage is too extensive to patch

body: A good patch is flat, feathered wide, and textured to match. Damaged board is cut back to solid material and backed so the new piece is firmly supported. Joints are taped with the right tape for the location, then built up in several progressively wider coats so the repair does not leave a hump that catches afternoon light.

Texture matching is where many repairs give themselves away. Orange peel, knockdown, and hand textures are tested on scrap board first and adjusted until they match before they go on the wall. The repair is primed so it absorbs paint the same way as the surrounding surface, then painted. Usually we paint the full wall or ceiling plane so there is no visible edge.

sections.h2: Cracks that come back are telling you something
body: A crack that reopens every year is usually a symptom, not the problem. Cracks where the wall meets the ceiling often come from roof trusses moving with temperature and humidity. Diagonal cracks off door corners can point to settlement. Filling these with more mud just means paying for the same repair again next season.

On the walkthrough, the crew lead looks at the pattern and tells you what is likely going on before quoting. Some joints need a flexible or floating detail rather than a rigid patch, and a few situations call for a structural or roofing professional first.

Nail pops follow a similar logic. Fasteners back out when framing lumber dries and shrinks, which is common in our climate as homes cycle between humid summers and drier winters. Mudding over the head leaves a bump that returns. The right fix is to drive a new screw beside the popped fastener to pull the board tight, set the old one, then fill and feather the spot.

After a leak, wet drywall has to dry fully, and moisture readings tell us whether it has. Board that stayed wet too long, sags, or crumbles is replaced instead of patched. Stains are sealed with a stain-blocking primer so they do not bleed back through the new paint.

Bubbling or blistering paint is often a moisture or prep issue hiding under the finish. Our guide to fixing bubbling paint on drywall covers the common causes. Damaged face paper from old wallpaper is another frequent repair, and is handled as part of our wallpaper removal service.

sections.h2: Repairs as part of a larger paint project
body: Many drywall repairs are folded into a room repaint or a whole-home interior painting project, since prep days already include filling nail holes and fixing pops. If you have leftover paint, we can work from it; if not, we color match from a chip or a painted surface with full-size drawdowns. Ceiling damage combined with dated texture is often best handled with ceiling refinishing instead of spot patches. Labelled touch-up paint is left with you when we finish.

We do not publish prices because every repair differs. The estimate depends on how many areas need work, their size, whether texture must be matched, how high the damage sits, and how much surrounding surface must be repainted to blend. A few anchor holes in one room is a short visit; a ceiling soaked by an AC overflow can mean cutting out board, drying, rehanging, taping, texturing, priming, and repainting the room. Your itemized quote spells out each repair and product so nothing is a surprise.

faqs.q: Can you match my existing wall texture?
faqs.a: Yes. We test the texture on scrap board and adjust until it matches before applying it to the repair, then prime and paint the area.

faqs.q: Will I see the patch after it is painted?
faqs.a: The aim is no. Repairs are feathered wide and primed, and we usually paint the full wall or ceiling plane so there is no visible edge or sheen difference.

faqs.q: Why does the crack over my door keep coming back?
faqs.a: Recurring cracks usually come from movement, such as truss uplift or settlement. A rigid patch will crack again, so we explain the likely cause and the right repair before quoting.

faqs.q: Do you fix drywall after a leak?
faqs.a: Yes, once the source is repaired and the board has dried. We check moisture, replace board that is damaged, seal stains, and repaint.
